newsitem.title: USA: Ellen DeGeneres nominated for Emmy Award.
newsitem.headline: Ellen DeGeneres nominated for Emmy Award.

text.p: Ellen DeGeneres, who made television history by coming out as a lesbian in her series "Ellen", was nominated for an Emmy award for best actress in a comedy series on Thursday.
The Home Box Office cable station led the nominations list with 90 nods, followed by NBC with 89, CBS with 60, ABC with 44 and Fox with 19.

The hospital drama "ER" received the most nominations with 22, followed by "The Larry Sanders Show" with 16. "The X-Files" and the cable television miniseries "Miss Evers' Boys", tied for third place with 12 nominations each.
"N.Y.P.D. Blue" was in fourth place with 11 nominations.
DeGeneres' best actress in a comedy series nomination was one of five for "Ellen", including best directing for a comedy series and best writing.

The show, however, did not receive a nomination for best comedy series -- those went to "Frasier", "The Larry Sanders Show", "Mad About You", "Seinfeld", and "Third Rock From the Sun". The hit series "Friends" was not nominated for best comedy, although it was erroneously mentioned as a nominee in a nationally televised nominations announcement.
DeGeneres' show triggered a national controversy earlier this year, when both the actress and her on-air character announced that they were gay.
The shows nominated for best drama series were hospital dramas "Chicago Hope", and "ER", police dramas "Law & Order" and "N.Y.P.D. Blue", and science fiction drama "The X-Files".
